_comment: Bridge variant: 12 m window at 8 cm voxels
Why this exists. On the 2 m baseline the model confuses abutments with pillars:
31.6% of abutment points are predicted as pillar, and 47.8% of everything predicted
'pillar' is really abutment. Both are vertical concrete; the only cue separating them
is WHERE in the structure they sit. The model cannot use that cue -- stencil.py centres
coordinates per block, and the three 'spatial' channels are density/anisotropy/local
structure, not position. Measured, abutments span 23-59 m in XY against a 2 m window.
Sizing. With cover tiling the effective per-block density is block_size / window^2, so
widening the window alone thins every block -- which is exactly the confound that sank
the earlier 2 cm experiment (E7, 60.37) in reverse. The voxel grid is therefore widened
WITH the window so density is preserved:
12 m window, 8 cm grid -> 142 pts/m^2 per block against 224 available (1.6x subsample)

Only the window and the voxel grid differ from domains/bridge.json. aug_preset stays 'strong' so this measures context alone -- 'strong_no_flip' exists for a separate test, since mirroring may teach the wrong end-vs-middle cue, but changing both at once would leave the result unattributable.
